title: Indri's Diwali 2026 Collector's Edition: Ruby Port Cask, 600 Numbered Bottles
excerpt: The fourth annual Diwali release from Piccadily Distilleries matures in Portuguese Ruby Port casks, arrives with Double Gold at the USA Spirits Ratings, and is limited to 600 numbered bottles for India.
body:
• Piccadily Distilleries has launched the Indri Diwali Collector's Edition 2026, a Ruby Port Cask single malt bottled at 50% ABV and restricted to 600 individually numbered bottles for the Indian market.
  • The expression arrives with heavyweight credentials: Double Gold with 96 points at the USA Spirits Ratings 2026, where it was also named Indian Single Malt Whisky of the Year and Spirit of the Year – India, plus Gold medals at competitions in London, New York and Singapore.
  • The 2023 edition of the series was named "Best Whisky in the World" at the Whiskies of the World Awards — a win widely credited with putting Indian single malts on the global map.
  • The 700 ml bottles go on sale in India from mid-October in Gurugram, Chandigarh and Bengaluru; a cask-strength 58.5% ABV variant will be available at duty-free outlets in Delhi, Mumbai, Hyderabad and Bengaluru, plus Dubai Duty Free.

A fourth Diwali chapter

Indri, the Haryana single malt that carried Indian whisky onto the world stage, is back with its annual Diwali statement piece. Piccadily Distilleries unveiled the Indri Diwali Collector's Edition 2026 in India on October 8, following the expression's international debut at The Whisky Show in London.

The 2026 edition is the fourth release in Indri's festive Collector's Edition series, and this year's cask choice is Ruby Port — hand-selected wine casks sourced from Portugal, into which whisky distilled from indigenous six-row Indian barley in traditional copper pot stills was matured in the subtropical climate of northern India.

The official tasting notes describe black cherries, wild berries and ripe plums on the nose, with a palate of honeyed fruits, roasted nuts, toffee, vanilla and figs — the red-fruit signature of Ruby Port showing through.

Awards before the India launch

The whisky reached India already decorated. Prior to its domestic release, the 2026 edition secured Double Gold with 96 points at the USA Spirits Ratings 2026, where it was also named Indian Single Malt Whisky of the Year and Spirit of the Year – India. Additional golds came at the World Whisky Masters 2026, the New York World Spirits Competition 2026 and the Asia World Spirits Competition 2026 in Singapore. The Collector's Edition series has now accumulated 29 international awards in total, according to The Hindu BusinessLine.

That track record rests on the 2023 edition's famous win: it was named "Best Whisky in the World" at the Whiskies of the World Awards, a recognition widely credited with elevating Indian single malts to global prominence and resetting expectations for what a tropical-climate whisky could be.

"The Diwali Collector's Edition has played a defining role in Indri's journey and in the story of Indian single malts globally."

— Surrinder Kumar, Master Blender, Piccadily Distilleries

Packaging and where to buy

The packaging was designed by Krsnaa Mehta of India Circus, drawing on Indian miniature art and royal heritage — jewel tones and ornate detailing built around a Marwari horse and foal. Like previous editions, the bottle is designed to be kept long after it is empty, which is the point: this is a collectible first and a drink second.

For the Indian market, 600 individually numbered 700 ml bottles at 50% ABV will be available from mid-October across Gurugram, Chandigarh and Bengaluru, priced as a premium collectible. An international variant bottled at a cask-strength 58.5% ABV will be offered at select duty-free outlets in Delhi, Mumbai, Hyderabad and Bengaluru, as well as Dubai Duty Free. In the UK, 180 bottles have been allocated at £200 through specialist retailers.

What it means

Indri's rise has been the defining business story of Indian spirits in this decade. A distillery in the village of Indri, Haryana — founded as a sugar and distillery business — now commands waitlists and auction-level interest for its limited releases. The Diwali series, in particular, has become a barometer of Indian luxury consumption: gifting-grade, culturally specific, and unapologetically premium.

For the diaspora, the timing is the news: bottles will be findable in Dubai Duty Free and the big Indian airports over the festival season — the gifting sweet spot for Diwali trips home.

What's next

With four editions banked and 29 international awards, the question for Piccadily is scale: whether Indri's limited-release magic can be sustained as production grows and global demand rises. The 2027 edition — and the cask Surrinder Kumar picks for it — will be watched closely. For this year, 600 numbered bottles for a country of 1.4 billion will not last long.
